1

Scope

This part of lSO/l EC 7816 specifies the physical characteristics of integrated circuit(s) cards with contacts. It applies to identification cards of the ID-I card type which may include embossing and/or a magnetic stripe as specified in lSO/lEC 7811-1 to lSO/lEC 7811-6. This part of lSO/l EC 7816 applies to cards which have a physical interface with electrical however, define the nature, number and position of the integrated circuits in the cards.

to this part of 1S0/1EC 7816 or will result in the need for other International Standards to be prepared.

references

4 Physical

characteristics

The following physical characteristics describe the card after the insertion of integrated circuit(s) with contacts into an ID-1 card type meeting the requirements of lSO/l EC 7810. Such a card may also meet the requirements of lSO/lEC 7811 -;"to lSO/lE~ 781 l-6"and lSO/lEC 7813. Test methods are described in lSO/lEC 10373. 4.1 General specified for all types of identification cards in lSO/lEC 7810 shall apply to IC cards.

The physical characteristics

NOTE The thickness of the cards as specified in lSO/lEC 7810 applies to a non-embossed card including contacts and integrated circuits. NOTE 2 Concerning "resistance to chemicals" (see subclause 8.1.4 of lSO/lEC 7810: 1995) the attention of card issuers is drawn to the fact that information held on a magnetic stripe or in the integrated circuit(s) maybe rendered ineffective as a result of contamination.

Additional Ultra-violet

characteristics light of the card manufacturer.

Any protection 4.2.2 X-rays

beyond the ambient UV light level shall be the responsibility

Exposure of either side of the card to a dose of 0,1 Gy of medium-energy (cumulative dose per year) shall not cause malfunction of the card.
NOTE 4.2.3

X-radiation

of 70 keV to 140 keV

This corresponds to twice the generally accepted human dose of 0,05 Gy per year.

Surface

profile of contacts

No point of the IC contact surface shall be higher than 0,05 mm above or lower than 0,1 mm below the adjacent surface of the card. The protection area specified in subclause 9.2.2 of lSO/lEC 7810:1995 shall be extended to the area between B and C shown in figure 3 in lSO/lEC 7810:1995. 4.2.4

Mechanical

strength

(of cards and contacts) contained in it and should remain intact during

The card should resist damage to its surface and to any components normal use, storage and handling.

Each contact surface and contact area (entire galvanic surface) shall not be damaged equivalent to a steel ball of diameter 1 mm applying a force of 1,5 N. 4.2.5 Electrical resistance (of contacts)

by a working

pressure

The impedance shall be such that the voltage across the impedance current of 10 mA peak at a frequency of 4 MHz. 4.2.6 Electromagnetic interference

shall remain lower than 10 mV for an a.c.

[between magnetic stripe and integrated

circuit(s)]

If the card carries a magnetic stripe, the K card shall not be damaged, malfunction or be altered after reading, writing or erasing of the magnetic stripe. Conversely, the writing or reading of the integrated circuit(s) shall not cause a malfunction of the magnetic stripe or its associated reading, writing or handling mechanisms. 4.2.7 Static electricity in normal use by a person charged with static electricity. any contact and

The integrated circuit shall not be damaged

The performance of the card shall not be degraded by exposure to a static discharge between ground of a voltage of 2000 V through a resistance of 1500 Q from a capacitor of 100 pF. 4.2.8 Operating temperature range between O "C and 50 `C.

Standards are also reviewed periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is tAken up for revision.
